knowledgePoint.title: Solving Rational Equations with Binomials in Both Denominators

response.solution:
First, we note that

- $x=-\frac{1}{2}$ cannot be a solution since this would make the denominator on the left-hand side zero

- $x=-1$ cannot be a solution since this would make the denominator on the right-hand side zero

We can flip an equation involving two fractions as follows:

$$
\frac{a}{b}=\frac{c}{d}\,⟹\,\frac{b}{a}=\frac{d}{c}
$$

The above technique works whenever $a$ and $c$ are both different from zero.

Therefore, we can flip the given equation as follows:

$$
\frac{2x+1}{5}=\frac{x+1}{1}
$$

Next, we write both fractions using the least common denominator, $5.$ The equation becomes

$$
\frac{2x+1}{5}=\frac{5x+5}{5}.
$$

We can now solve this equation with the addition and the multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}(5)\cdot \frac{2x+1}{5} & =(5)\cdot \frac{5x+5}{5} \\ 2x+1 & =5x+5 \\ 1-5 & =5x-2x \\ -4 & =3x \\ \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)\cdot (-4) & =\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)\cdot (3x) \\ \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)\cdot (-4) & =(\cancel{\frac{1}{3}})\cdot (\cancel{3}x) \\ -\frac{4}{3} & =x\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that the solution is $x=-\frac{4}{3}.$
